comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C1, C2, C14-C16, C23-C24 about benign nature of RP tumors as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites histological data and prior work; peer reviewers accept this as established background contextualizing the current study.

Strong disagreement. OpenEval finds claims C17-C18 (TP53/RB1 loss alone produces benign tumors while MYC addition produces metastatic disease) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether MYC might render RB1/TP53 loss dispensable and requesting additional experiments to test necessity of all three alterations.

Agreement with acknowledged limitations. Both evaluate metastasis-related claims (C3, C19-C20, C36-C38, C78) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes site-specific requirement and quantitative data. Peer reviewers affirm this as the major finding but note limitations regarding metastasis frequency and anatomical sites.

Agreement on DOX-dependence. Both find claims C25-C29 about tumor growth kinetics and DOX withdrawal/add-back experiments SUPPORTED. These claims overlap with peer result R1's broader evaluation of the metastatic phenotype as convincingly demonstrated.

Agreement on histological findings. Both find claims C30-C33 about histological characteristics SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the microenvironment inference (C33) is speculative but reasonable; peer reviewers accept these as part of the model characterization.

Disagreement on interpretation. OpenEval finds claims C86-C87 (site-dependence of metastasis) SUPPORTED, appropriately framing C87 as speculation. Peer reviewers rate C87 as UNCERTAIN, explicitly critiquing this as a significant limitation that reduces how well the model recapitulates widely metastatic human SCLC.

Disagreement on completeness. OpenEval finds claims C79-C83 (rationale for MYC overexpression design) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers rate C80-C83 as UNCERTAIN, noting the MYC-specific focus is a significant limitation and that impact would increase with testing of MYCL and other family members.

Agreement on SCLC-N classification. Both find claims C73-C77 about subtype enrichment and SCLC-N characteristics SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the MYC-driven transformation inference is correlative; peer reviewers accept the subtype classification as key model characterization.

Agreement on SCLC-N subtype. Both find claims C4, C84 about SCLC-N classification SUPPORTED. OpenEval bases this on comprehensive transcriptional profiling; peer reviewers acknowledge this finding without challenge as part of model characterization.

Agreement on marker expression. Both find claims C42-C44 about NEUROD1/ASCL1 expression patterns SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanistic validation is lacking for C44; peer reviewers accept gene expression analyses showing these markers.

Agreement on metastatic lesion characteristics. Both find claims C40-C41, C46 about comparative analysis between primary and metastatic sites SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes immunohistochemical data; peer reviewers accept these findings without methodological concerns.

Agreement on paired sample analysis. Both find claims C5-C6 about NEUROD1 expression in primary and metastatic lesions SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limited sample size; peer reviewers accept this as part of model characterization without raising concerns.

Agreement on molecular validation. Both find claims C21-C22 about western blot validation of DOX induction SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriateness of experimental validation; peer reviewers treat this as straightforward validation without concerns.

Agreement on MYC specificity. Both find claims C54-C57 about MYC family member specificity SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes high statistical significance; peer reviewers accept expression analyses without question, though R8 separately notes broader MYC family testing as a limitation.

Agreement on scRNA-seq clustering. Both find claims C47, C50-C51 about single-cell clustering and cell type identification SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate methodology; peer reviewers accept these findings without methodological concerns.

Agreement on cluster abundance. Both find claims C52-C53, C58 about differential cluster abundance analysis SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes highly significant p-values and EGFP+ sorting consideration; peer reviewers accept computational analyses without challenge.

Agreement on sub-clustering analysis. Both find claims C61-C64 about differential gene expression in subclusters SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical support but unclear functional significance of some pathways; peer reviewers accept these molecular characterizations.

Agreement on cell cycle analysis. Both find claims C65-C67 about increased proliferation in MYC-expressing cells SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes highly significant p-values and consistency with phenotype; peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Agreement on MYC-NEUROD1 correlation. Both find claims C68-C72 about correlation analyses SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong correlation but cautions about sample size; peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting evidence.

Agreement on neuroendocrine marker expression. Both find claims C59-C60 about NEUROD1/ASCL1 expression in subclusters SUPPORTED. These overlap with peer reviewers' acceptance of gene expression analyses showing neuroendocrine characteristics.

Agreement on clustering methodology. Claim C48 about clustering approach overlaps with peer acceptance of gene expression analyses. Both find the analytical approach SUPPORTED without methodological concerns.
Agreement on MYC-SCLC-N link. Claim C72 about MYC linking to SCLC-N phenotype overlaps with peer acceptance of SCLC-N classification. Both find this inference SUPPORTED based on correlative data.

Agreement on negative finding. Both find claim C39 (absence of metastases in certain organs) SUPPORTED. OpenEval appropriately frames this as observation rather than definitive conclusion; peer reviewers note this as part of the limitation regarding metastatic sites.

Agreement on immunohistochemical markers. Claims C35, C45 about marker expression overlap with peer acceptance of the metastatic phenotype characterization. Both find these SUPPORTED as part of model validation.

OpenEval finds claims C11-C13 (established prior work and SCLC background) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these appear to be accepted as background context.

OpenEval finds claims C7-C10 (historical and technological context) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these provide general background rather than specific findings under review.

OpenEval finds claim C85 (acknowledgment of uncertainty about MYC role in SCLC) SUPPORTED as honest discussion of field limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this relates to the broader concern about MYC specificity raised in R8.
